objective: Find which sections of HolyAgent's agent prompts are needed only at a specific moment and could move into skills that trigger then, without overdoing it.
scope: The instruction sources in packages/runtime/src/instructions/claude-5.5/ (the root sections under root/, every specialist prompt, shared sections, session-reminder.md) and how the generated plugin assembles them (packages/integrations/claude/src/agents.ts and the dist/agents/*.md output). Existing skills: packages/runtime/src/instructions or packages/integrations/claude skills folders (dev-server, user-busy, setup).

For each candidate: the section and file, its size in words, the moment it is needed (the trigger a skill description would name), how often that moment comes up, and whether the agent's main job depends on it every turn (then it stays in the prompt).
constraints: Be conservative: propose a skill only for text that is needed at a specific moment rather than on most turns and is not the core reason the agent exists. Say for each rejected large section why it stays.

Keep working until the analysis is done, then stop and report under 600 words, with a ranked list of at most 8 candidates and the word count each would remove from the always-loaded prompt. Each evidence entry on one line as '<criterion label>: <support>'.

criteria.text: Candidates: each proposed skill names its source section, word count, trigger moment and which agents lose the text
Kept sections: the large sections that stay are named with the reason

result:
result: 7 candidates; moving them out of the always-loaded root cuts about 1,780 words, and moving the design guidance out of two specialists cuts about 2,100 more. The `wc` tool was unavailable, so all word counts are estimates (about ±10%) from reading the generated `dist/agents/*.md` files. I did not read the `root/` source files individually; I used `dist/agents/holyagent.md`, which assembles them in the order set in `packages/integrations/claude/src/agents.ts` (`ROOT_SECTIONS`). The root is the only agent with the Skill tool among those that would lose text.

**Assembly facts**
- The root prompt is the 15 `root/*.md` files joined in order. The root loads skills with the Skill tool.
- Specialists get the role files, the five `specialist/` sections, and the conditional sections (`merge-ready`, `writing-bar`, `interface-inspection`), assembled in `agents.ts`.
- Only `reviewer-code` and `reviewer-security` have the Skill tool, because the other specialists deny it. A specialist skill therefore needs a tool-grant change in `builtinsOf` and `denylist`.
- Test `REQUIREMENT_SECTIONS` ties each requirement to a phrase in a named source file. Text that moves must be re-mapped, or the test fails.

**Ranked candidates**

| # | Candidate | Source | Words | Trigger | Frequency | Loses it |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `visual-judging` | `root/visual.md` ("Judging visual work") | ~370 | Rendered or UI work reaches acceptance, or a visual finding or repair round starts | Only UI tasks | root |
| 2 | `ci-watch` | `root/ci.md` | ~290 (plus ~35 `root/pr-text.md` as a stretch) | A branch is pushed and its PR opened, or a CI result needs reading | Once per delivery, only with a remote | root |
| 3 | `stack-plan` | `root/stack-plan.md` | ~380 | Planning branches and PRs for a multi-PR delivery, or merging forward | Per delivery; trivial on a single PR | root |
| 4 | `instruction-writing` | `root/instruction-guidelines.md` | ~330 removed (of ~540) | Writing or reviewing agent prompts, skills, instruction files or workflow prompts | Rare, maintenance-type work | root |
| 5 | `state-mode` | "State:" bullet in `root/version-control.md` | ~170 | Once per clone, before the first Intent, or when `holyagent state mode` reads unset | Once per clone | root |
| 6 | `ask-user` | `root/asking.md` | ~280 (keep the one-line "ask only when material" rule in the core `task-list.md`) | About to ask a decision, or the user asks what needs their decision | Some sessions | root |
| 7 | `frontend-design` | `FRONTEND_DESIGN_SECTION` (appended from the vendored `frontend-design` skill) | ~1,050 per agent | Building or reshaping a new interface (worker), or judging a new or reshaped interface (reviewer) | Only UI tasks; small bug repairs and capture-only runs do not need it | worker-visual, reviewer-visual |

For #4, the part to keep in the prompt is what is needed to write an Assignment brief: the full-task bullet, the keep-working and stop-and-report bullet, and the real-check bullet. The root writes a brief on every dispatch, so those bullets stay.

For #7, `packages/integrations/claude/vendor/frontend-design/SKILL.md` already exists, so no text is new. It is the largest single saving but also the riskiest. Both agents need the Skill tool, and a skipped load silently drops the design bar. The visual agents' tool lists and the test mapping for `R-RV-DESIGN` and `R-WVI-DESIGN` change with it. Treat it as optional: do #1 to #5 first.

**Rejected as too small**
- `worker-operations/dev-server.md` (~130 words, one agent). A skill's description would cost nearly as much, and Worker.operations cannot load skills.
- `worker-debugging/escalation.md` (~70 words). Too small to be worth a skill.
- The "Where to look" list in `interface-inspection.md` (~220 words). Too small for a split.

**Kept sections**
- `specialist/merge-ready.md` (~560 words, 7 roles). Every writer and code or testing review applies it each turn, and it is their criteria bar.
- `specialist/working.md`, `scope.md`, `state-changes.md`, `report.md`, `conduct.md` (~700 words in all 18 agents). They are the conduct of every turn, and the report format is machine-matched.
- `specialist/interface-inspection.md` (~520 words). It is the core method of the two visual agents.
- `specialist/writing-bar.md` (~150 words). It is small and is the writing bar for instruction-text work.
- `root/assignments.md` (~700 words). Dispatch and acceptance run every turn.
- `root/version-control.md` outside the state bullet (~390 words). Commits happen on most deliveries.
- `root/workflows.md` (~700 words). Every dispatch is a workflow script, and the script rules gate permission.
- `root/user-messages.md` (~330 words). It applies to every message, and its noise list fires in every session.
- `root/routing.md`, `context.md`, `search.md`. Routing is per dispatch, and `context.md` carries the report-cap rule.
- The core (`identity`, `delegating`, `dispatch`, `task-list`, about 750 words). `ROOT_CORE` is also reused as-is for non-root sessions.
- The role method files (`reviewer-security` trust boundaries, `reviewer-code`, `worker-implementation` and the like). They are the agent's reason to exist.
- `session-reminder.md` (~60 words). It is a deliberate short restatement.

**Gaps**
- I did not read `requirements.md` or the tests, so the exact mapping updates are unverified.
- Word counts for `reviewer-artifact` and `worker-implementation/instruction-text.md` are estimated from the generated files, not the sources.

notes: Each skill adds a description of about 40 words to the always-loaded prompt, so the net saving for #5 and #6 is smaller than listed. The `dev-server` and `user-busy` pointer lines in `root/skills.md` would also extend to cover each new skill.
